core_obligations: For an affine open Spec(A), use dimension zero plus Noether normalization to get a finite injection k to A, hence finite k-dimension, hence A Artinian and a product of finitely many Artinian local rings of finite k-dimension (proof lines 3745-3757).

Conclude that X is covered by finite discrete spaces, hence is discrete, and therefore is the disjoint union of its singleton connected components, each the spectrum of a local Artinian k-algebra of finite dimension (proof lines 3759-3766).

In the algebraic case, use quasi-compactness to write X as a finite disjoint union of such spectra, which is affine, and recall the finiteness of X over Spec(k) from the first paragraph (proof lines 3768-3775).
proof_roadmap: Analyse an affine open by Noether normalization (proof lines 3745-3757).
Show X is discrete and decompose into singletons (proof lines 3759-3766).
Handle the algebraic case by quasi-compactness (proof lines 3768-3775).
difficulty_reason: For a locally algebraic k-scheme X of dimension zero, the lemma shows that X is a disjoint union of spectra of local Artinian k-algebras of finite k-dimension and that in the algebraic case X is affine with X to Spec(k) finite (statement lines 3735-3742). The proof examines an affine open Spec(A): dimension zero of X gives dimension zero of A, Noether normalization then produces a finite injection k to A so that A has finite k-dimension, hence A is Artinian and therefore a product of finitely many Artinian local rings (proof lines 3745-3757). Since these are finite discrete spaces, X itself is discrete, so X is the disjoint union of its singleton connected components, each of which is the spectrum of such an algebra (proof lines 3759-3766). The algebraic case then uses quasi-compactness to write X as a finite disjoint union of such spectra, which is affine, and finiteness of X to Spec(k) was already seen (proof lines 3768-3775). The claim is H2: four standard algebra facts chained together, with no step referred to the reader.
